source.author: verg
source.text: Hinc metuunt cupiuntque, dolent gaudentque, neque auras dispiciunt clausae tenebris et carcere caeco.
source.text_original: Hinc metuunt cupiuntque, dolent gaudentque, neque auras / dispiciunt clausae tenebris et carcere caeco.
source.text_english: From this they fear and desire, they grieve and rejoice, and do not discern the air, shut in by darkness and a blind prison.

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: Has perturbationes uno et nec pleno versiculo illustris poeta comprehendit: Hi metuunt cupiuntque hoc de futuro , dolent gaudentque hoc de praesenti neque auras, inquit, Respiciunt, clausi tenebris et carcere caeco.
reuse.text_original: Has perturbationes uno et nec pleno versiculo illustris poeta comprehendit: Hi metuunt cupiuntque ( hoc de futuro ), dolent gaudentque ( hoc de praesenti ) neque auras, inquit, Respiciunt, clausi tenebris et carcere caeco.
reuse.text_english: This famous poet encompassed these disturbances in a single, and not full, line: They fear and desire this from the future, they grieve and rejoice at this from the present, and, he says, they do not look to the breezes, shut in by darkness and blind prison.
